en: The Great Sūtra on the Ritual for the Accomplishment of the Bodhisattva Ārya-Krodhavajrakumāra,
Volume One. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master and Śramaṇa Da Guangzhi of Daxingshan Monastery.
Translated by Amoghavajra by Imperial Decree. At that time, the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi rose from his seat,
prostrated at the Buddha’s feet, withdrew to sit on one side,
joined his palms toward the Buddha, and addressed the Buddha, saying:
The World-Honored One has out of compassion empowered me and has already taught the ritual procedures, regulations, and doctrines for the *Susiddhi* mantras.
I now wish [to explain them] for the sake of future sentient beings and those lacking merit during the age of the final dharma.
Because they failed to cultivate wholesome qualities and committed various sinful deeds in previous lives,
they have now experienced poverty and destitution in this life, encountered wicked people,
engaged in strife and litigation, and brought harm to sentient beings.
Furthermore, for the sake of future kings who rule their nations with the True Dharma and give rise to pure faith and reverence for the Triple Gem,
[I shall do so] lest neighboring minor kings invade their borders and fail to follow the True Dharma.
There may be non-Buddhists who do not believe in cause and effect,
who slander the Triple Gem, and who destroy the Buddha's teachings;
there are various sentient beings such as these.
Now, before the Buddha, for the sake of those various classes of beings,
I shall expound these methods for pacifying, increasing, magnetizing, and subjugating,
so that they may come to know that the Buddha-dharma possesses great majestic power and sovereign supernormal faculties.
They know that all bodhisattvas are endowed with omniscience;
or again, there are those who practice the conduct of mantras and observances who see sentient beings constantly harboring malicious intentions.
Desiring to destroy the Buddha-dharma and raise an army to harm the virtuous,
he was moved by great compassion and performed a rite of subjugation,
thereby causing that person's evil karma not to succeed.
It also prevents future falls into the three evil destinies;
therefore, this ritual manual for the incomparable, highly virtuous, noble Krodhavajrakumāra is taught.
One who practices this dharma should do so before a stupa containing relics,
or by the bank of a river with clear, flowing water.
Whether in a secluded place, a temple, or among the mountains—
in such locations as these—
he may at times drink milk and eat vegetables, or else subsist on alms.
If one recites the mantra exclusively for six hundred thousand times,
all previously performed rites will achieve accomplishment and possess great efficacy;
or one may bind, strike, and interrogate [spirits], and all matters will be as desired.
It subdues all malevolent spirits and demons;
it eradicates wrong views and those who slander the True Dharma;
and it destroys those who ruin the nation, such as the icchantikas and their like.
The power of the mantra is such that it can cause all those beings to give rise to a virtuous mind;
poisonous insects and green herbs cannot harm them.
Furthermore, other practitioners of various mantra recitations will be unable to subvert this dharma.
If there is a practitioner who,
while reciting, is unable to follow these rules exactly—
whether by adding or subtracting— they shall still attain fulfillment.
Furthermore, it can open all hidden treasures and break the bolts of the asuras;
it can dry up rivers and cause flowing waters to turn back and cease.
Moreover, there is the preliminary ritual procedure.
Take one's own *rūdrākṣa* beads and *gorocanā*, mixing them with clarified butter (*sarpis*).
Then, offer a thousand lamps to the noble Vajrakumāra.
Having made the offering, [proceed].
A voice from the sky spoke these words:
"Your dharma is now perfected;
you may now take this arghya perfumed water and offer it upon your forehead."
From this point forward,
may all things you seek be accomplished without exception.
Furthermore, if you wish to go to the palace of the asuras to experience sublime delights, [may it be so].
When approaching the entrance of the asura cave, one should fashion a hook from *kuśa* grass.
Recite the mantra of Vajrakumāra seven times to empower the grass hook,
and then rotate it clockwise in the air beside the gate.
Recite the mantra single-mindedly without interruption;
a great mass of fire will then arise within the cave,
and all the asuras, both male and female, therein shall be consumed by its flames.
Weeping in terror and making "ha-ha" sounds,
each of the asura women shall manifest her body and address the reciter, saying:
I only pray that the Venerable One will enter my cave and sport there as you please.
Once you have entered,
may you dwell there for an eon, enjoying the sublime pleasures of the heavens.
Furthermore, if one wishes to retrieve a hidden treasure (*nidhi*),
one should not discriminate against the lunar day, the week-day, or the time, nor need one immediately observe the fast and precepts; rather,
one should stand at the side of that hidden treasure with one foot raised and recite the mantra.

Turning one's gaze clockwise to survey all four directions, one thereby establishes the boundary; when constructing a great maṇḍala, this same method is employed: standing with focused mind and feet raised, recite the mantra one hundred and eight times.
Within that treasure cache, the guardian of the treasure,
if he creates obstacles or difficulties, will immediately be burned into a single mass of fire;
then, weeping, he shall come before the practitioner, kneel in prostration, and submit.
The reciter shall then say to them:
"Open this treasure-store;
whatever is within it, give all of it to me."
They shall then open [the treasure] for the practitioner.
If they are stingy and do not give it, one should speak these words:
"Brahmā, Nārāyaṇa, Maheśvara, the Goddess of Battle, the Nāgas, and others shall come to suppress and subdue your hidden treasure."
"You should quickly give this object to me.
If you do not, the wrathful noble Vajrakumāra will destroy your family.
When they heard these words, they...
They all submitted in obedience and spoke thus:
"Venerable sir, please take whatever you desire;
we have no reluctance."
He then said to them,
"You may open the treasury yourselves and give it to me.
They then opened the treasury and respectfully brought it to him.
Furthermore, there is another method: take realgar, orpiment, ox-gall, or añjana eye-salve,
and place it in a vessel made of gold, silver,
or refined copper before a stūpa containing relics.
Anoint one side of the altar with incense.
Place an image of the Noble Vajrakumāra in the center of the altar.
Offer various kinds of incense, flowers, food, and argha water.
Having invited [the deity] according to the instructions, one should make offerings to them.
Before this mandala, one should recite the mantra eight thousand times with single-minded focus.
By consecrating the aforementioned medicine, the three signs will then manifest.
These are known as the signs of warmth, smoke, and light.
If the sign of warmth appears,
one should apply it to the forehead or smear it into the eyes.
All people who see him will become attached to him and feel joy in their hearts.
If the sign of smoke appears,
by using it as before, one will attain the accomplishment of *āveśana* (possession).
If one sees the manifestation of light signs as before,
one will immediately attain the power to fly through space with mastery.
Furthermore, there is a method [to practice] at the Ganges River or a river that flows into the ocean.
One who performs recitation by the side of this river—
whether consuming pure food or fasting— should recite the mantra three hundred thousand times until reaching the cave of the asuras.
By forming the mudrā and reciting the mantra,
the bolts of the asura’s cave naturally broke,
and the entrance to the cavern opened immediately.
The Asura King leads him into his palace,
where he partakes of celestial ambrosia (amṛta) and lives for one kalpa.
Furthermore, according to the Dharma, if one is by the shore of a great ocean...
Forming the mudrā and reciting this mantra over the great ocean water,
the water immediately recedes by twenty-five cubits;
wherever it recedes, the ground becomes parched dry.
Furthermore, there is another method:
at the edge of the seashore, close one's eyes and block both ears with cotton;
form the mudrā and recite the mantra one thousand times.
Immediately, one sees oneself arrive at the summit of Mount Laṅkā.
Furthermore, if one recites [the mantra] a thousand times,
there will appear the Rākṣasa King Māyāviśana.
Manifesting a majestic and beautiful body, he approaches the practitioner;
he sustains the reciter and dispatches him as a servant. If he does not submit to being employed as a servant, [the practitioner must employ other means].
The practitioner should visualize that Rākṣasa beneath his left foot;
as he lifts his foot to step upon the ground,
the Rākṣasa king faints and dies.
The city of Laṅkā where they dwell is entirely consumed by fire like a great mass of flames;
the reciter should then arouse a mind of compassion.
If one adds the word *svāhā* to the mantra phrases,
those rākṣasas and others will immediately find relief;
they will submit to the practitioner and may be employed as servants at will.
Furthermore, there is another method: before Kumāra, while mounted upon the peacock deity, one should recite the mantra three hundred thousand times without eating.
Kumāra will then immediately manifest his body.
He grants his vow before the practitioner.
The practitioner then takes the argha perfumed water and recites the mantra over it seven times while empowering it.
And making this offering, he spoke these words:
"Welcome, Kumāra!
May I attain accomplishment in all the mantras taught by the god Kumāra-Maheśvara."
Kumāra said, "May you achieve success.
Having spoken these words, he vanished from sight.
From this point forward, all mantras spoken within the Vajra Family as well as by other deities shall be accomplished.
Furthermore, there is a rite for proceeding to the temple of the deity Maheśvara.
If one recites the mantra one hundred thousand times while fasting,
all that the heart desires shall be fully realized.
Furthermore, there is a method [for propitiating] Brahmā, Nārāyaṇa, Maheśvara, Śakra Devendra, Kumāra, and Sūrya.
Before the images of any other deities,
if one recites the mantra one hundred thousand times,
whatever wishes one has in mind will all be fulfilled.
Furthermore, there is another method: before the entrance to an asura cave where a practitioner has previously entered for practice, one should recite the mantra one hundred thousand times.
This refers to a practitioner who has already achieved mastery through recitation within that cave.
Emerging from the cave, he comes forward to welcome [the deity], receives him upon his head,
and leads him into the palace of the asuras;
if he does not come, then [he is brought] to the temple of Maheśvara.
Reciting the mantra while simultaneously uttering the syllable *HŪṂ* one thousand times,
the first person who had entered the Asura palace shall emerge from the cave;
this applies likewise to the second, third, and up to the seventh person.
They all came forth and spoke these words:
"We previously entered the palace of the Asura King Kharaṭika;
it was solely by upholding the mantra of Vajrakumāra that we were able to enter this palace."
Out of mutual affection and longing, we have formed a friendship.
We shall all join in shaming and punishing anyone who does not welcome you.
Together with you, we must not enter the cave of the asuras.
Then, in front of the cave, he took the withered flowers offered to Maheśvara and also took the painted image of Maheśvara;
he then stepped upon its head with his left foot.
If one performs homa by casting withered flowers into the fire,
Śrīdevī will become a companion to the asura women;
emerging from her cave, she will come before the practitioner and speak these words:
One must never accept those who serve as attendants; rather,
one should recite the mantra with a voice like a thundering roar of wrath.
They were all utterly deluded and frantic;
they stripped off their own garments until their bodies were naked.
Then the goddess Śrī and the asura women spoke these words:
"We serve the Venerable One.
The practitioner claps three times and says, "Follow me."
Immediately generating a mind of loving-kindness,
he added the syllable *svāhā* to the mantra phrases;
those who were bewildered and fainting all regained their senses.
If, while performing this rite, one does not enter [the state],
the practitioner should close their eyes and recite the mantra eight times;
then the noble Vajrakumāra will manifest his form and speak to the practitioner, saying:
"Come, my son.
Enter the asura cave and go to the second gate;
the gate shall open of its own accord."
If one enters oneself, one’s retinue and others shall likewise all be able to enter.
By performing this rite, one will gain access to all seven kinds of palaces belonging to the asura kings.
Furthermore, if one wishes to subdue wicked people,
take mustard seeds and mix them with salt;
perform the homa while reciting the mantra one hundred thousand times.
If one recites that name once and casts mustard seeds and salt into the fire,
even the devas and asuras shall be destroyed.
How much more so for other human beings;
how could those who give rise to malicious intent not be destroyed?
Even though they previously possessed no meritorious deeds, [they shall still be harmed].
Success is achieved with every recitation;
how much more so for one who constantly upholds it.
Furthermore, if one wishes to transform the *Mṛḍika* into gold and precious jewels, [the following method applies].
Take a mṛttikā (clay) and place it upon his head with the left foot;
strike him with the mudrā while reciting the mantra syllables together with the syllable HŪṂ.
Mṛḍika then rose up of his own accord;
[the king] struck him with a sword made of puṣpa-iron,
whereupon his entire body was transformed into a golden form.
If it is not so, the reciter shall say, "Quickly eject! Quickly eject!
and it will immediately eject the wish-fulfilling jewel (cintāmaṇi).
Hang it from beneath one's neck;
all matters one contemplates will be fully accomplished.
Furthermore, according to another method, one should recite the mantra six hundred thousand times before a Śarīra stūpa.
First, one should accomplish the preliminary rites. Then,
one should fashion a sword from *puṣpa* iron,
measuring six finger-widths, eight finger-widths, sixteen finger-widths, or thirty-two finger-widths in length.
Alternatively, one may follow the measurements for the sword found in other mantra teachings.
Once the sword has been completed, wash it with the five purifiers.
Holding the sword in the right hand, perform recitation within the maṇḍala.
When the sword even manifests blazing flames,
the practitioner of recitation attains the transformation of body,
becoming a vidyādhara who soars through the void.
He is named the Vidyādhara Sword-Bearer.
Alternatively, one may fashion a vajra from *puṣpa* iron,
its dimensions as described in the Subāhuparipṛcchā Sūtra.
Reciting as before,
one’s body is transformed into that of the Vidyādhara Lord of the Vināyakas,
attaining mastery over all the hosts of māras.
Alternatively, if one performs the recitation while forming the wheel as before,
one becomes a Wheel-bearing Ṛṣi and attains mastery over all Vidyā-ṛṣis.
If one performs the recitation while forming the battle-axe as before, [the same result follows].
One may also transform into the sage who is the lord of the Vināyakas;
if one performs the recitation with the axe as before,
one will then transform into the sage who is the lord of the ghosts and spirits.
One attains mastery over all ghosts and spirits.
If one fashions a knife, one becomes a celestial queen and a rishi,
attaining sovereign power over all celestial maidens.
If one forms the pāśa mudrā, one becomes a lord of nāgas and a ṛṣi,
attaining mastery over all nāgas.
If one forms the śakti mudrā, one obtains valor, strength, and great power.
One can rival the god Kumāra;
if one performs the khaṭvāṅga [posture],
one attains a state like that of Maheśvara.
One attains mastery within the three realms;
if one accomplishes even a single one of the aforementioned dharmas,
one is immediately able to enter all maṇḍalas.
They are also able to accomplish all dharmas;
they travel together with the vidyādhara sages,
and their lifespan is one great kalpa.
Furthermore, for one who wishes to be protected by Śakra, Lord of the Devas,
take the dung of seven earthworms and fashion it into the form of that deity;
then, step upon its heart with the right foot.
Take poison, *halāhala*, and white mustard seeds;
recite the mantra one thousand times and perform the *homā* while reciting the mantra.
If one recites it once and casts it into the fire,
one will gain the respect and affection of Śakra, Lord of the Devas,
and his celestial retinue will constantly come to provide protection.
Furthermore, there is a method: if one recites the mantra seven times over flowers or fruits and bestows them upon others, they will attain joy.
This mantra of Vajrakumāra should be recited before a stūpa containing relics.
In other places, one should not perform recitation;
the ritual will not be accomplished.
However, if one recites constantly without interruption, [the result will be attained].
All that is sought shall be accomplished.
One should resolve upon the bodhicitta and abandon thoughts of stinginess;
one should constantly practice relinquishment and give alms, remaining far removed from worldly talk that is without benefit.
All supreme vows shall manifest before them;
they shall not be susceptible to the influence of any māras,
nor should they treat the illnesses of others.
Furthermore, regarding the subjugation of malevolent spirits that obstruct the Great Dharma,
I shall now explain the fundamental mudrā for the sequence of mantra recitation, mudrās, and rituals of the Noble Krodhavajrakumāra.
As for the mudrā: join the two middle fingers back-to-back and extend them upright;
cross the two ring fingers horizontally across the outer side of the middle joints of the middle fingers;
and hook the tips of the two index fingers around the tips of the two ring fingers.
Place the tips of the two thumbs against the middle joints of the two middle fingers;
join the tips of the two little fingers and point them downward like needles, and it is thus formed.
The Root Mantra is as follows:
Namaḥ ratnatrayāya | Namaḥ śrīvajrapāṇaye mahākṣapate | Tadyathā | Oṃ kaṇi viduṇi hūṃ phaṭ svāhā || Furthermore, the second root mantra is as follows: [followed by the same sequence].
To open the palace of the asuras,
use the aforementioned root mudrā.
The mantra is as follows:
Namaḥ ratnatrayāya | Namaḥ śrīvajrapāṇaye | Maheśvara-kṣetrapataye | Tadyathā | Oṃ dudunāma vidudunāma kaṇi kuru dhā | Sarvāntarani | Hūṃ || Next, perform the single-pronged vajra mudrā.
Interlace the two hands within to form fists;
interlock the two thumbs over the tips of the two little fingers.
With the index fingers held upright and joined together, one completes [the mudrā] using the aforementioned first root mantra.
Next, bind the body-protection mudrā.
Using the previously mentioned root mudrā,
seal the five places of the body.
The mantra is:
Oṃ sarva-nu-stha va-kha-ka-ra-ka-ṇi ku-ru dhā-ra kṣa rakṣa maṃ svāhā. Next, perform the armor-binding mudrā.
Following the previous root mudrā, extend the two index fingers so that they touch at their tips.
Then, press the two thumbs against the first joints of the two index fingers; thus it is formed.
Seal the five places of the body.
The mantra is:
Oṃ hrīḥ kaṇi yama no ha hūṃ phaṭ svāhā. Next, bind the Jewel Mountain mudrā.
Following the previous single-pronged mallet mudrā,
slightly bend the tips of both index fingers so that they touch each other;
placing them upon the head completes it.
The mantra is:
Oṃ āḥ jra hūṃ. Second, for the mudrā of the boundary wall, follow the previous root mudrā.
Simply extend the two index fingers straight,
with their tips about one inch apart, and it is accomplished.
The mantra is as follows:
Oṃ hrīṃ kaṇi noha noha paca paca hūṃ phaṭ. Next, perform the net mudrā (*jālamudrā*).
Following the previous root mudrā, extend the two index fingers outward; this completes it.
The mantra is as follows:
Oṃ phaṭ. Next, perform the seal for binding the vināyakas.
It is based on the previous root seal:
bend both index fingers and both middle fingers into the palms.
Place each of the two thumbs over the middle fingers;
with the nails joined back-to-back within the palms, form a fist.
The mantra is as follows:
Oṃ namo bhagavate śūramahābalāya sarvaviṣanāśakāya hūṃ svāhā. Next, perform the mudrā for inviting the Noble One.
Following the previous root mudrā,
form it by beckoning toward oneself with the two thumbs.
The mantra is as follows:
Oṃ dūṇī phaṭ. Next, bind the mudrā for inviting the retinue of the noble ones.
Use the previously mentioned mudrā for welcoming;
the mantra is as follows:
Oṃ sabārivāra-ma-vāhaya-mahā. Next, perform the *argha* offering mudrā.
Following the previous root mudrā,
form it by pressing the two thumbs against the first joints of the two index fingers.
The mantra is as follows:
Oṃ vajradhara nāga hūṃ. Second, perform the mudrā for offering the seat.
This follows the single-pronged vajra mudrā, with the two thumbs pressing the first joints of the two index fingers.
It is accomplished by turning the head slightly outward.
The mantra is:
Oṃ vajravīra svāhā. Third, perform the mudrā for offering scented ointment.
Following the previous single-pronged mallet mudrā,
slightly bend both thumbs and press them against the first joint of the index fingers.
When the two thumbs are separated by a distance of approximately two inches, it is accomplished.
The mantra is as follows:
It can fulfill whatever ritual procedures may be deficient.
The mantra is:
Oṃ kaṇikuruḍa sarvasattvān pūjara pūjara sarvavandani svāhā. Next, perform the flower-offering mudrā.
Form the seal of the single-pronged mallet as previously described;
it is completed by extending the right thumb.
The mantra is as follows:
Oṃ gaṇipuṣpa mu na bha va hūṃ. Next, perform the incense mudrā.
Following the previous procedure for the single-pronged mace mudrā, join the two thumbs face-to-face;
this constitutes the mantra, which is as follows: Oṃ kaṇi kuru-dha ugra-ṇeṣṭaru de-kṣaṭa pe-ra-ba agra-haṇa agra-haṇa du-bhuṃ svāhā. Next, perform the food offering mudrā.
Following the previous single-pronged mallet mudrā,
extend the two thumbs and touch the tips of the two little fingers together.
Interlace the remaining six fingers within to form a fist, and it is thus completed.
The mantra is:
Oṃ kaṇi hūṃ hūṃ svāhā. Next, perform the lamp-lighting mudrā (*dīpamudrā*).
Following the previous method for the single-pronged mallet mudrā,
extend the two index fingers toward the body and hold them both upright; thus it is formed.
The mantra is:
Oṃ kaṇipadapadya hūṃ phaṭ svāhā. Next, perform the head mudrā.
Following the previous root mudrā, press the two thumbs against the tips of the two ring fingers; this completes it.
The mantra is as follows:
Oṃ hūṃ hūṃ ma ma phaṭ. (Recite three times. Then, form the crown mudrā according to the previous root mudrā.
Extend both index fingers straight upward with their tips touching, and it is thus formed.
The mantra is:
Oṃ hrīḥ caṇḍakani naho bhañja hūṃ phaṭ svāhā. Next, bind the previously mentioned root mudrā.
Rest it upon the heart.
Consecrate the heart with the Heart Mantra.
The mantra is as follows:
Oṃ kaṇi hūṃ phaṭ. Next, form the Armor Mudrā (Kavaca-mudrā).
It is formed like the mudrā of Bodhisattva Tārā;
simply slightly opening the two index fingers completes it.
Using the aforementioned armor mantra,
next form the Supreme Seal:
interlace the two hands with palms facing inward to form fists.
The two little fingers joined together form [the mudrā].
Then, using the aforementioned second root mantra,
hold the rosary at the heart.
Consecrate [the offerings] seven times with the *Cittavajra* mantra.
The *Cittavajra* mantra is:
Oṃ ka ni du ma hūṃ phaṭ. Next, form the mudrā for sending off the Noble One.
Following the previous root mudrā, extend the two index fingers outward; this completes it.
The mantra is as follows:
Oṃ kaṇi svāhā. I shall now further explain the mudrā for opening the door of the asura cave.
The reciter should act with haste;
he should step upon the ground with leaping and bounding, or with trepidation;
he should yawn, knit his brows, and puff out both cheeks.
Raising both hands high, he bends the ten fingers to form the "lion's claws.
His two eyes look downward like a lion’s backward glance.
From time to time, he forms the lion's claws with both hands.
Moving up and down alternately,
they touch the ground as they walk like lions;
performing the *ariṣṭa-sthita* dance, they circumambulate.
Visualize oneself as the deity.
This mudrā is the most supreme among all mudrās;
it can destroy the bolts and pivots of all the palaces of the asuras.
Vajragarbha Bodhisattva said:
"I shall now explain the method for painting the image of Vajrakumāra.
One should take an uncut piece of white cotton cloth and remove all hair and down."
The painter must observe the eight precepts while painting the body of the Bodhisattva,
adorning it with various kinds of necklaces and ornaments.
His body is the color of fire, with flames streaming forth from all over his form.
With his right hand he holds a vajra, raised upward at an angle;
his left hand is in the mudrā of granting boons (varada-mudrā).
With his feet in the *ālīḍha* stance, he stands upon a stone pedestal;
beneath his hand in the boon-granting (*varada*) gesture, one should paint the practitioner,
kneeling on the right knee and holding an incense burner in his hand.
Once the image has been completed,
one should perform various kinds of offerings before it,
burning frankincense while reciting the mantra without interruption.
Even until signs of accomplishment appear:
one hears a voice from the sky and the sound of bells;
furthermore, light appears, like a shooting star.
It fell into the mandala with a sound like a thunderclap.
Immediately at that spot,
one should offer arghya using the perfumed water from the kumbha of excellence (bhadraghaṭa) that was previously placed there.
If the image moves or emits light,
one should know that the practitioner of recitation has achieved efficacious results.
Thereafter, perform the recitation before this image.
Whatever matters one desires will all be fully accomplished.
Furthermore, the method for painting the image is explained as before.
Take a piece of white cotton cloth that has been woven but not yet cut;
wash it with cow's urine and then rinse it with scented water.
In a secluded place or before the Buddha, [perform the rite].
Whether at a stūpa containing relics or within a meditation hall,
one must not use hide-glue mixed with pigments;
the painting brushes, colors, and bowls must all be new.
The painter must bathe and purify himself.
Wearing fresh, clean garments and observing the eight precepts of purification,
he shall close his mouth and swallow his breath, ensuring that no exhaled air strikes the image.
Furthermore, one should not deliberate with that painter regarding the price of the work;
rather, they should reach a mutual agreement to reward his labor.
That image [depicts] a single figure emerging from the great ocean.
His body is the color of lapis lazuli;
he has six arms, which are well-proportioned and full in appearance;
his face has three eyes, and these eyes are red in color.
He wears a jeweled crown with canine fangs protruding upward;
he bites his lower lip with a frowning brow in a posture of fierce wrath.
Furthermore, within the ocean, paint a single jewel mountain.
The image stands with its left foot treading upon a jewel mountain,
atop which a wondrous lotus of various colors supports that foot;
the right foot stands in the seawater, submerged up to the mid-knee.
The first right hand holds a *triśūla* vajra in a throwing gesture;
the second right hand holds a *musala* club,
meaning a staff with one end shaped like an iron *kīla*.
The right third hand holds a battle-axe;
the left first hand grasps a staff;
the left second hand forms a vajra-fist in a threatening gesture with the index finger extended; and the left third hand holds a sword.

casting one oblation into the fire with each recitation.
All the messengers of Maheśvara are completely subdued and brought under command;

taking pieces of *khadira* wood ten finger-widths long.

begin the homa ritual on the fourteenth day of the waxing moon;

Recite the mantra one thousand and eight times,
casting it into the fire once for each recitation.

dip it in ghee, honey, and curd,

at each session, recite the mantra one thousand and eight times,
casting [the offering] into the fire once for every recitation.
One will immediately achieve the subjugation of all yakṣas.
Furthermore, if one wishes to summon a yakṣiṇī,

providing all necessary clothing, food, drink,

with each recitation of the mantra, cast [a portion] into the fire.

casting one portion into the fire with each recitation.

when speaking to others, whatever is requested shall be obtained according to one's wishes.

One will achieve victory over enemies and not be subjected to their oppression.
Furthermore, there is a method: burn one hundred thousand pellets of frankincense (*agaru*) while performing *homa* and reciting the mantra without interruption.
One will immediately obtain one hundred thousand coins.

spreading bodhi leaves in a clockwise direction.
Place the sword upon a leaf and recite the mantra.
When light is emitted, offer argha water as an offering to the *iṣṭadevatā*.
Holding the sword with the right hand, one will attain the manifestation of the three signs.
Then, together with a thousand people and their various retinues,
they simultaneously soared into the void and arrived at the palace of the Honored One.
If one travels to the palaces of the vidyādhara sages,
none shall be able to obstruct or destroy [one's progress];
together with one's retinue, one shall likewise attain a lifespan of one million years.
Furthermore, there is a method: take sweet flag (*achyranthes aspera*) and perform *homa* offerings.
Recite the mantra one thousand and eight times, casting one piece into the fire with each recitation.
One will immediately obtain wealth and treasures.
Furthermore, there is a method: take a banner and consecrate it one hundred and eight times with the mantra.
Then, offer incense, flowers, and seven bowls of curd to the banner, and present *argha* water.
Then, carrying this banner, lead the army forward; when the enemy army sees the banner, they will break apart of their own accord.
Furthermore, if a city or town has been seized, one should perform *homa* for seven days before an image using yellow flowers.
Every day before the image, recite the mantra one thousand and eight times;
with each recitation, cast [a portion] into the fire.
If a city has previously been seized by an enemy force, [this shall restore it].
Then they shall all be repelled.
Furthermore, one should perform the preliminary rite (*pūrvasevā*).
Taking white mustard seeds, perform *homa* for seven days and seven nights; within one month, treasures will rain down upon that dwelling.
Furthermore, there is a method: kindle a fire with *śrīvṛkṣa* wood and perform *homā* before the image,
reciting the mantra one thousand and eight times.
Recite the mantra once and cast it once into the fire;
one will immediately obtain hidden treasures or attain great wealth.
Furthermore, there is another method: before the image, extensively arrange offerings.
Take incense and flowers, smear them with clarified butter (*ghṛta*), and perform a *homa* offering.
Recite the mantra one hundred thousand times,
casting one portion into the fire with each recitation.
One will immediately obtain wealth and treasures.
Furthermore, there is a method: place an image before a śarīra-stūpa and perform homa with one hundred thousand stalks of blue lotus flowers.
Recite the mantra one hundred thousand times;
with each recitation, cast [a portion] into the fire.
One will immediately obtain a manor estate.
Furthermore, according to another method, one should perform offerings of incense and flowers before the image.
The practitioner should subsist on milk and eat barley,
and take one thousand and eight stalks of lotus flowers, dip them in ghee, and perform *homa* oblations.
Recite the mantra one thousand and eight times;
with each recitation, cast [an offering] into the fire, and you shall obtain one thousand taels of gold.
Furthermore, there is another method: before the image, take one hundred thousand stalks of red lotus and perform homa.
Recite the mantra one hundred thousand times,
casting it into the fire once for each recitation;
whatever one seeks in one's heart shall be entirely attained.
Furthermore, if one desires to seek office,
one should take ten thousand white flowers, dip them in ghee,
and perform homa while reciting the mantra ten thousand times.
Recite the mantra once and cast [the substance] into the fire once;
one will immediately attain high advancement in official rank and emolument.
Furthermore, there is another method: perform *homā* with powdered iron.
Recite the mantra ten thousand times;
for each recitation, take a pinch [of the substance] and cast it into the fire.
One will immediately obtain one thousand gold coins.
Furthermore, there is a method: take saffron and smear it with fragrant oil, then perform *homa*.
Recite the mantra one hundred thousand times, casting a small amount of the mixture into the fire with each recitation.
It can fulfill all supreme aspirations.
Furthermore, there is a method: take all kinds of incense and perform homa while reciting the mantra one hundred thousand times.
Each time he threw [the image] once into the fire,
the cities and towns seized by a neighboring kingdom were immediately recovered.

Recite the mantra one hundred thousand times, casting one piece into the fire with each recitation.

All diseases shall be entirely cured.

All those who are imprisoned or bound shall obtain liberation.

first empower the incense seven times and then offer it.

The youth faces west. As for the mudrā,
one forms fists by interlacing the two hands with the palms facing inward,
and hooks the two little fingers together.
With the two thumbs held upright side by side,
pinch them together in the shape of a hook-lock and place them firmly upon the forehead.
The boy and girl then spoke,
and with their two thumbs they pushed outward;
the boy immediately retreated and walked far away.
The two great fingers point toward the body;
as the youth immediately comes forward, he is summoned.
Wave the mudrā to the left and right.

when the seal was raised upward, the youth stood up at once.
He was asked about matters of good and ill fortune throughout the three periods of time, and every single thing was found to be true.

The accomplisher of all deeds, the wrathful king of great power,

the asura kings and their retinues, Maheśvara and Nārāyaṇa, the nāga kings,

the practitioner should enter the samādhi of the Wrathful King.

Now I shall further explain the mantra for empowering objects to be accomplished through the seal (*mudrā*) that can fulfill all purposes when seeking *siddhi*. It is as follows:
Oṃ kaṇi kuruḍa sarvasattvabandha sarvanaraviṣaṇi svāhā. [This is the mudrā for washing.]
Following the previous method for the single-pronged mallet mudrā:
join both thumbs together inside the palms and bring the wrists together; thus it is formed.
The mantra is:

Oṃ kaṇi kuruḍa sarvasattvabhāvyapraṇāmanākāre siddhime pradyeṣa svāhā. The mantra for sweeping the ground of the ritual site is: [Oṃ kaṇi kuruḍa sarvasattvabhāvyapraṇāmanākāre siddhime pradyeṣa svāhā].
Oṃ kaṇimāraya hūṃ. This is the mudrā for binding those who are difficult to subdue when seeking accomplishment.
Following the previous root mudrā,
interlace the two thumbs within the palms to form it.
The mantra is:
Oṃ kaṇiścarṣaya sarvanuśveta mandadhaya mandadhaya hūṃ phaṭ. This is the Great Vajra Heart Seal.
Following the previous method for the single-pronged vajra mudrā,
interlace the two thumbs within the palms;
this constitutes the Mahāvajra-yathāmanas-kāra-mudrā.
Following the previous heart-seal (hṛdaya-mudrā),
it is formed by holding the two thumbs upright side-by-side;

The Supreme Heart Seal:
Following the previous Supreme Seal,
bend the two little fingers.

If the heads [of the hands] are pressed together, this mudrā is formed. Should various obstacles arise or inauspicious events occur within the home, by binding this mudrā and reciting the mantra, they will all be dispelled.

Following the previous *jyeṣṭha-mudrā*,
extend the two ring fingers and the two little fingers, and it is accomplished.
This mudrā can accomplish all tasks.
If one enters the palace of the asuras,
this seal likewise possesses great power.
Next, the Great Hook Seal is explained.
Interlace the two hands with the palms facing inward;
bend the two index fingers like hooks, and it is thus formed.
This mudrā [subdues] all classes of sentient beings within the three realms.
One can summon them all.
If it is an asura woman,
she will come immediately upon hearing the summons within seven days.
Furthermore, the Gaṇakī mudrā is described as follows:

Interlace the remaining six fingers within and extend the two thumbs to count;

Not only does it dispel the ḍākinīs,

For this mudrā, one should employ the root mantra.
Furthermore, it is said that for the seal of subduing all nāgas,

but bend the thumbs and insert them into the palms.
Place the two thumbs facing each other directly.
Visualize that the dragon is formed within the joint of the thumbs;
this mudrā can subdue all dragons and is used for praying for rain or stopping rain.
All nāgas, upon seeing this seal, will regard it as the garuḍa;

Interlace the two inner hands and join the two thumbs face-to-face;

Furthermore, there is a method: perform homa by burning various incenses.

Sitting before the image upon its form,

at each session, recite the mantra one thousand and eight times.
All the devas, nāgas, and the eight classes of spirits summoned shall come to serve as messengers, and all tasks will be accomplished.
Furthermore, there is a rite: perform *homa* with salt mixed with mustard seeds for seven nights.
Recite the mantra separately one thousand and eight times, and great enemies will be immediately subdued.

Recite the mantra one thousand and eight times, and all that is sought shall be attained.
Furthermore, there is another method: take a discarded used tooth-stick, ignite it as fire, and [proceed].
Take one thousand and eight *karavīra* flowers—known as *kunāvi* flowers by those people to the south of the ridges—and perform a *homa* offering by anointing them with clarified butter (*ghṛta*).
Recite the mantra one thousand and eight times.
Reciting it once and casting it once into the fire, one immediately achieves the subjugation of all things.

To obtain elixirs for longevity, *anuttara* medicines, magical swords, hidden treasures, gold, silver, and the seven precious jewels,

One will protect oneself and one's companions so that all attain unimpededness;

and whatever is sought shall be accomplished.

the names of the generals and those below them shall each be empowered seven times with the mantra.

they will not be harmed and shall achieve victory.

one should recite the mantra one hundred and eight times before the image to empower it,
and pour [the liquid] over the crown of the head.
That person, whether reciting for themselves or for others,
may have long exerted effort yet fail to achieve manifest results, becoming afflicted by various māras and tormented by inauspicious spirits and demons.
By performing this rite of consecration and ablution,
all malevolent spirits and demons shall be utterly driven away;
one's merit and virtue will blaze forth, and swift accomplishment will be attained.
Furthermore, there is a method: by consecrating scented water one thousand and eight times with the mantra and sprinkling it upon the body, all ghost-induced fevers shall be cured.
Furthermore, there is a method: at a secluded place on the bank of the Ganges River.
One should fashion one thousand and eight sand stupas,
each as high as the span of the Tathāgata’s hand,
and offer worship before them according to one's ability.
Before each stupa, one should recite the mantra one thousand and eight times;
thus, one will attain mastery of supernatural powers and great wealth and honor.
Furthermore, there is another method: place an image before a stupa containing relics.
Recite the mantra one thousand and eight times, and all that is sought shall be attained.

If a person has been poisoned,
brush their body with a peacock’s tail [empowered by the mantra].

as well as *gomaya* (cow dung) that has not yet fallen to the ground.

upon that altar, extensively arrange offerings.

one will obtain one thousand silver coins as well as a manor estate.

For the sake of the benefit, welfare, and happiness of all sentient beings,

Those who possess pure faith and delight in practicing the Mahāyāna,
as well as those who are indolent and lazy and lack wisdom and skillful means,
should swiftly accumulate merit and wisdom and cultivate the practice of mantra and conduct.
May he act as a sovereign king who protects and upholds the True Dharma,

Do not harbor doubts; practice according to the Dharma.
I shall now explain the ritual for consecrating iron (puṣpa-loha-vidhi). Iron from ship nails; iron from battle-weapons such as armlets and ornaments worn on the limbs of men;

iron from hairpins; iron from chains; iron from children’s armlets; iron from grass-bands worn on the bodies of elephants; iron from elephant-tusk spikes; iron from bed-nails and bedstead nails; iron from battle-swords that have wounded men; iron from door-nails; iron from plowshares; iron from the handles of parasols; iron from medicine mortars; iron from horse bits; iron from foot-rings; iron from arrowheads; and iron from celestial chariots—each of these types of iron should be taken in equal proportions, melted together, and forged into vajras, wheels, hooks, swords, axes, hatchets, and *bheruṇḍas*. Chains should be made with a length equal to one span (*vitasti*) of the Tathāgata.
The *pātra* (bowl) is twelve finger-widths (*aṅgula*) in length;
the *vajra* (thunderbolt) is sixteen finger-widths long, and the *aṅkuśa* (hook) is twelve finger-widths long.
The *cakra* (wheel) measures one span (*vitasti*) in size, and its circumference is surrounded by flames.

Realgar: five *liang* for the superior grade, five *liang* for the middle grade, three *liang* for the inferior grade, and one *liang* for the lowest grade; other medicines are to be adjusted accordingly.
Cow bezoar: one *liang*.
Yellow orpiment: two *liang*.
Take three parts of milk and seven *liang* of clarified butter (*ghṛta*).
Grind them with the five pure substances (*pañcagavya*).
Grind realgar and orpiment with milk; grind cow bezoar (*gorocanā*) with clarified butter.
Sprinkle the ghee with scented water.
*The Sūtra of the Vidyārāja Krodhavajrakumāra Āryakāṇi*, Scroll II.
